title: CHIPS NAPMP Final Advanced-Packaging Awards
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: NIST announced $1.4 billion in final advanced-packaging awards: $100 million each to Absolics, Applied Materials, and Arizona State University, plus $1.1 billion to Natcast for advanced-packaging capabilities at the Tempe prototyping and piloting facility.
key_findings: Three $100 million awards target glass-core substrates, silicon-core substrates, and wafer or panel-level processing.
The $1.1 billion Natcast award is intended to operate advanced-packaging capabilities co-located with NSTC prototyping in Tempe.
The planned facility includes a baseline advanced-packaging piloting line intended to bridge laboratory research and production.
why_it_matters: The awards identify recipients, locations, facility functions, and targeted manufacturing capabilities behind the Phase 55K semiconductor-equipment and packaging direction.
ftfn_relevance: Adds named awards and facility intent to the advanced-semiconductor-packaging technology profile.
Creates follow-up gates for tool installation, access, pilot-line operation, process qualification, and commercialization.
evidence_limits: Final awards do not prove the facilities or piloting lines are operational.
The source does not establish process yields, qualified products, customers, production volumes, or commercial transition.
